items.problem: When a `Guild` poll on the way succeeds after a `load_older` of that channel ended with `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER` (`_check_not_member` at line 773 raises `w.epoch`), lines 669-671 set the next poll to `_failure_retry_ms`. `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/chat-core.md:87` sets `poll_after_ms` when the previous request succeeded. Run path: `watch_channel(GUILD, 0)`, poll pending, `load_older` gets `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER`, the poll response arrives with `poll_after_ms` smaller than `ChatCore.failureRetryMs`. The effect is only a later next request. This code is not in the commit range

The `w.busy` branch of `_on_sent` (`w.kick`, and lines 682-685 of `_send_poll`) has no test. `chat-core.md:106` requires the poll to go right after a send, and without this branch a message sent during a poll waits for the next `poll_after_ms`. In `client/godot/core/chat_core/tests/`, `test_send.gd` holds no response pending, and the only pending `GET_MESSAGES` that coexists with a send (`test_channel_poll.gd:162`) belongs to `load_older` and ends with `release` before a send result. Removing the branch fails no test by reading the tests; this was not run. This code is not in the commit range

`load_older` ending with `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER` has no test, and neither has the `epoch` branches that drop results after that reset (lines 669 and 768). `chat-core.md:93` applies to any request of a `Guild` channel, and the only test with that error is the poll in `client/godot/core/chat_core/tests/test_watch.gd:93`. Removing `_check_not_member` at line 773 fails no test by reading the tests; this was not run. This code is not in the commit range

`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/chat-core.md:75` raises the read seq when a watched channel receives messages, and `chat-core.md:179` requires a test that its unread becomes 0, but no test goes through the poll path. `test_a_watched_channel_that_receives_messages_has_no_unread` (client/godot/core/chat_core/tests/test_watch.gd:67) receives its messages only in the first request (chat_core.gd:696). Run: removing the `_raise_from_cache` call at line 723 in a temporary copy and running `ogw core test godot ChatCore` gives `ChatCore pass`. With that defect, a channel open on screen shows a growing unread count for each message that arrives by poll

`chat-core.md:79` and `chat-core.md:173` require a `[chat_badge]` item with the current unread count, and no test changes the count of an item that stays at 1 or more. Run: reducing the condition at line 607 to `not _badge_items.has(item)`, so that an existing item is not updated, gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run, see `## unknown`). With that defect, the badge keeps the first count while unread rises

`chat-core.md:88-92` sets the poll order `Removed` then `Appended`, and no test has one poll response with both `deleted_seqs` and new messages. `test_deleted_seqs_leave_the_cache_with_a_removed_event_of_that_count` (test_watch.gd) has no new messages in that response. Run: moving the removal block after the append block gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run)

`chat-core.md:65` sends nothing until `release` after `CHILD_RESTRICTED`, and no test has a poll on the way when the restriction arrives. `test_child_restricted_stops_every_request_until_release_init_and_start` (test_channel_poll.gd) holds no poll pending. Run path with no test: a `Guild` poll is pending, `GetChatChannels` ends with `CHILD_RESTRICTED`, the poll response has another `channel_key`. Run: removing `and not _restricted` at this line, which then sends a first request after the restriction, gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run)

`chat-core.md:93` resets the cache only on `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER`, and no test has a `Guild` request fail with another error. The only `Guild` request failure asserted is `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER` in test_watch.gd. Run: removing the error code condition at lines 736-737, so that any failure empties the cache, gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run). With that defect, one `INTERNAL` or timeout on a guild poll empties the chat on screen

`chat-core.md:93` publishes `Reset`(0) only when the cache had messages, and no test has `GUILD_NOT_MEMBER` on an empty cache. Run: publishing whatever the cache held gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run). With that defect, a watched `Guild` channel of a user without a guild publishes `Reset` every `ChatCore.failureRetryMs`

`chat-core.md:65` publishes `ChatChannelsChangedEvent` on `CHILD_RESTRICTED` only when the list changed, and no test has `CHILD_RESTRICTED` with an empty list. test_channel_poll.gd reaches it only with a list of one item. Run: publishing always at this line gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run)

`chat-core.md:94` discards the results of requests in progress on `unwatch_channel`, and no test calls `unwatch_channel` while a `load_older` is in progress; test_watch.gd holds only a poll pending. Run: removing the `wait.fire(false)` loop at lines 287-288 gives `ChatCore pass` (combined run). With that defect, the `load_older` of the caller never returns

`_apply_older` puts received messages in the cache but does not raise the read seq, so a watched channel whose cache was empty keeps its unread count and its `[chat_badge]` item after it receives messages. `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/chat-core.md:75` raises the read seq to the largest seq of the cache when a watched channel receives messages, and `chat-core.md:179` requires its unread to become 0. Only `_apply_first` (line 696) and `_apply_poll` (line 723) call `_raise_from_cache`. With a non-empty cache this has no effect, because `load_older` adds only smaller seqs. It needs a first response with no messages and `first_seq` above 1: the server selects the newest `chat.maxFetchCount` rows and leaves out deleted messages and those of blocked senders, so all of those rows can be hidden while older visible messages are unread. Reproduced with a probe test in a temporary copy, run with `ogw core test godot ChatCore`: saved read seq `CHAT_CHANNEL_KIND_DIRECT:501=2`, list item `last_seq` 60 and `last_visible_seq` 5, first response with no messages, `last_seq` 60 and `first_seq` 11, `load_older` response with seqs 4 and 5. The cache is then [4, 5], `get_unread_count` is 3 where 0 is expected, and the `[chat_badge]` item count is 3 where 0 is expected. The code is unchanged in the range
